page: Amazon Web Services z1d.metal is a bare-metal instance designed for memory-intensive workloads that require sustained high core clock frequencies. It is powered by custom Intel Xeon 8151 processors operating at 4.0 GHz across 24 physical cores and 48 vCPUs. The server provides direct bare-metal access to hardware without hypervisor overhead, supported by 384 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, 1,800 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD instance storage, and a 25 Gbps baseline network interface. It includes no dedicated GPUs.

Benchmark results highlight strong memory subsystem performance, positioning the host in the top 25% for uncached read throughput at 217.08 GB/sec and large block write throughput at 92.41 GB/sec. Its overall PassMark memory benchmark score also places in the top quartile. Compute benchmarks reflect mid-tier throughput, showing average scores across stress-ng single-core (1668.89) and multi-core (52885.51), Geekbench 6 multi-core (12108.0), and PassMark CPU evaluations (45079.06). LLM text generation speeds remain in the lower 25%, demonstrating that CPU-based transformer inference is inefficient compared to hardware-accelerated platforms.

The primary architectural advantage of z1d.metal lies in the density of its 8 GB per vCPU memory profile combined with a 4.0 GHz single-core frequency and integrated NVMe capacity. From a resource efficiency standpoint, workloads that carry high per-core licensing fees benefit substantially from the high clock speeds, maximizing per-core performance output. It is well suited for relational databases, in-memory data stores like Redis, electronic design automation (EDA), financial modeling, and data-heavy build processes requiring direct metal access.
description: Amazon Web Services z1d.metal is a bare-metal server configured for memory-intensive enterprise tasks demanding high clock frequencies. Built on an x86_64 architecture with Intel Xeon 8151 processors, it offers 24 physical cores and 48 vCPUs operating at a 4.0 GHz base frequency. The hardware configuration features 384 GB of DDR4 memory, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio, combined with 1,800 GB of integrated NVMe SSD storage and 25 Gbps network connectivity. The server does not include GPU acceleration. Benchmarks validate strong memory bandwidth performance, ranking in the top 25% for uncached read and write operations, alongside typical compute throughput in CPU-intensive tasks. This hardware profile delivers qualitative licensing efficiency for high-frequency relational databases, in-memory caches, electronic design automation, and intensive build workloads.
